Testimony ofRepresentative Anne-Marie Mastraccio presenting
LD 1150, An Act to Require Reporting of Sheltering or Aiding
Missing Children
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safely
Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus and esteemed colleagues on the Joint Standing
Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety, I am Anne-Marie Mastraccio, and I represent
House District 142, which includes part of the City of Sanford and part of the Village of
Springvale. I am before you today to present LD 1150, An Act to Require Reporting of
Sheltering or Aiding Missing Children.
This legislation proposes that a person who knowingly shelters a missing or runway child for
more than 24 hours without the consent of the missing child's parent or guardian must provide information regarding the missing child's location and condition to a law enforcement officer if
contacted and asked about the child. A person who violates this provision would be subject to a
civil penalty not to exceed $250.
It is not a crime in Maine to run away from home, nor is it against the law to harbor a runaway. I
am not proposing such a law. The teenage years can be trying for parents and teens and
sometimes a cooling off period can be helpful for all parties. If your 16-year-old decides to run away and ends up at someone else's home, you might suspect where they are but the adult in that
home is under no obligation to even confirm that fact. Sometimes all the parent needs to know is
that their child is safe and sheltered and not on the street. This bill would do that without forcing the juvenile to retum home, while still giving police the ability to assure the juvenile's safety and
location. I believe it would go a long way in alleviating the worry of a parent without creating an
atmosphere where the juvenile is treated like a criminal.
Thank you for the opportunity to present this bill and I look forward to a discussion on this
important issue.

My name is Judy Cohen and I am working for RSU 20 as the McKenney Vento liaison. I am a masters level Social Worker and have been employed in this district for over 30 years. I am in support of this bill for the following reasons. . .
1. Many youth over the years I have known through working in Maine Public schools for over 35 years do leave their home usually for good reason. 2. I think letting the parent of guardian know they are safe without forcing the child back to the home is a way to de-escalate the situation. 3. What I have done is always let the police know ahead what is happening as long as the teen isn't coerced by the police to return home.
A situation like this arose just yesterday. . . A 14 almost 15 year old special needs student left the home of her biological father because of the father's behavior which included becoming physical with her. Exactly what happened I must depend on what the student says. She went to a friend's home and called to tell me. I spoke to the friend's mom and let her know that she is doing nothing illegal and coached her what to say should the father or a police officer come to her apartment. The stepmom of the student who is no longer living with the father called the police proactively. So I have always done this or a functional adult in the student's life (like in this case) can do so.
My only concern is if the legal parent/guardian is violent or threatening perhaps they should be told that their child is safe but in some situations not be told where the child is staying in order to protect the host home and family.
